explanation:
[EFFECT]
Temperature has a strong, non-monotonic (inverted U-shaped) effect on predicted bike demand. Very cold temperatures (near 0 °C) drastically reduce demand, with contributions as low as −1.5 in log space. Demand rises steadily as it warms up, peaking around 31–33 °C (normalized temp ≈ 0.75–0.80), where the contribution reaches about +0.30. Extremely hot temperatures (above ~39 °C) also slightly suppress demand, though far less severely than cold weather.

[IMPORTANCE]
Temperature is the **second most important** feature in the model (rank 2 out of 9, importance score 0.253), meaning it is one of the strongest drivers of hourly rental demand, second only to the hour of the day.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan for significantly higher bike availability and staffing during mild-to-warm weather (roughly 18–33 °C), and reduce operational resources in cold or extreme-heat periods, since temperature swings create some of the largest swings in expected ridership.
